newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA REINFORCE NEW-LOOK SQUAD AFTER INJURIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA REINFORCE NEW-LOOK SQUAD AFTER INJURIES.

text.p: Injuries have forced Russia coach Boris Ignatyev to bring midfielder Alexei Kosolapov and defender Dmitry Khlestov into a new-look squad for Wednesday's World Cup qualifier against Luxembourg.
Kosolapov, 25, replaces Spartak Moscow's Ilya Tsymbalar, who is ruled out for at least two months by a knee injury.
Spartak's Khlestov, also 25, is a familiar face in the national squad and wins his place back at the expense of the injured Ramiz Mamedov.

Russia are looking for a much-improved performance in Moscow after being held to a 1-1 draw away to Cyprus in their last qualifier and Ignatyev responded by dropping some of his foreign-based players.
Ignatyev said Bologna striker Igor Kolyvanov, Celta Vigo midfielder Alexander Mostovoy and Valencia midfielder Valery Karpin had to give way to younger legs.

But critics say Ignatyev, who took over from Oleg Romantsev after Russia's disastrous performance at Euro 96, has bowed to popular discontent with foreign-based players whose commitment and patriotism have been questioned.
His 23-man squad includes first-time call-ups for in-form CSKA Moscow striker Vladimir Kulik and Alexander Gorshkov, a midfielder from this season's surprise early contenders Zhemchuzhina Sochi.
Also included are youngsters Vitaly Abramov from league leaders Rotor Volgograd and Sergei Grishin of Dynamo Moscow.
Rotor's Denis Zubko is back in the squad, and also recalled are Santander's Vladimir Beschastnykh and Zaragoza's Vladislav Radimov.

Yuri Nikiforov, a defender with good striking qualities but a poor disciplinary record, misses a second game in a row. Out, too, is Alania Vladikavkaz forward Anatoly Kanishchev, who was suspended after failing to show up in Cyprus.

The Russians beat Luxembourg 4-0 last November despite playing most of the match with 10 men. Russia are third in group five with eight points from four matches. Luxembourg are last with no points from four matches.
Goalkeepers - Sergei Ovchinnikov (Lokomotiv Moscow), Stanislav Cherchesov (Tirol Innsbruck)
Defenders - Dmitry Khlestov (Spartak Moscow), Maxim Bokov (CSKA Moscow), Igor Chugaynov (Lokomotiv Moscow), Viktor Onopko (Oviedo), Yuri Kovtun (Dynamo Moscow), Dmitry Popov (Compostela).

Midfielders - Andrei Kanchelskis (Fiorentina), Sergei Grishin (Dynamo), Omari Tetradze (Roma), Igor Yanovsky (Alania Vladikavkaz), Valery Kechinov, Dmitry Alenichev (both Spartak), Vitaly Abramov (Rotor Volgograd), Alexander Gorshkov (Zhemchuzhina Sochi), Alexei Kosolapov (Lokomotiv Moscow).
Forwards - Vladimir Kulik (CSKA), Denis Zubko (Rotor), Igor Simutenkov (Reggiana), Vladimir Beschastnykh (Racing Santander), Alexei Gerasimenko (Rostselmash Rostov), Vladislav Radimov (Zaragoza).
